content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after sharp price spikes in history.
- Model underreacts to downward trends; fails to adjust forecast downward when recent history shows mean reversion.
- Forecast mean is typically 1–2% higher than true outcome, suggesting a persistent upward bias.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent low prices; often holds forecasts too high even after price drops.
- Forecasts show excessive volatility relative to true outcomes, particularly in the middle of the 30d window.
- Model tends to overcorrect after sharp price reversals, leading to overshoots in the following days.
- Forecasts are less sensitive to the last 5–7 days of history, suggesting insufficient weighting of recent data.
